cohort: Women giving birth at an inner-city hospital network in Sydney, Australia, between August 1989 and December 2016
finding: The increased rate of cesarean delivery is mainly attributable to a greater number of procedures performed for slow progress in labor, breech presentation or repeat cesarean section.
mod_finding: The study found that the increase in cesarean delivery rates is largely due to more procedures being performed for slow labor progress, breech presentation, or repeat cesarean section.
